title: Smart Traffic
subtitle: Traffic services on the screen, and cameras on the road.
intro: The General Directorate of Traffic is one of the Ministry of Interior's sectors. Much of its work with drivers has moved to Absher, while automated monitoring now covers the most common violations on the road. This page sets those changes next to the road safety results published for 2016 to 2025.

items.title: Traffic Services on Absher
items.text: Renewing a licence, paying a fine, or transferring a vehicle no longer needs a visit: 3,432,289 traffic transactions were completed on Absher in November 2025 alone.

items.title: Automated Enforcement
items.text: The Ministry of Interior has expanded automated monitoring to more than 4,100 systems that detect speeding, seatbelt, mobile phone, and red-light violations.

items.title: A National Target
items.text: Road safety is part of Vision 2030, which aims to bring road deaths below 10 per 100,000 people by 2030.

items.caption: Night traffic on a Saudi highway

items.label: Road deaths in 2025, about half the 2016 figure

sections.heading: 2016 Against 2025
sections.note: A green badge means the figure went down. Each bar is drawn to scale against the larger year.

items.title: The starting point
items.text: When the National Transformation Program began, the road fatality rate was 28.8 per 100,000 people, higher than the average for low-income countries.

items.title: Halfway there
items.text: The Ministerial Committee for Traffic Safety's 2025 report puts the rate at 12.05 per 100,000, with deaths roughly halved since 2016.
